instructions:
This subtest contains 27 questions and assesses spatial reasoning using visual-based tasks.
Each question will be timed 45 seconds. Work quickly and carefully.
No external aids (notes, scratch paper, drawing tools, etc.) are allowed.
Make sure you follow these rules:
Your objective is to select exactly 3 options to reconstruct the given puzzle.
The selected pieces may be rotated, but they may not be flipped, altered in any other way, or overlap.

name: Spatial Awareness
instructions:
This subtest contains 23 questions and assesses spatial reasoning using language-based tasks.
Each question will be timed 45 seconds. Work quickly and carefully.
No external aids (calculators, notes, scratch paper, or drawing tools) are allowed.
Make sure you follow these directional rules:
Compass points follow the standard convention (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW).
Left = counter-clockwise; Right = clockwise.
A turn = 90 degrees.
A half turn = 45 degrees.

name: Quantitative Knowledge
seconds_per_question_note: per-item time is the item weight; DEFAULT_LIMIT=60 when unset
instructions:
This subtest contains up to 27 multiple-choice questions and assesses quantitative reasoning abilities.
Questions will be timed per item. Work quickly and carefully.
No external aids (calculators, Google, AI, etc.) are allowed. However, a formula sheet will be available during the test.
Pen and paper is strongly recommended for this subtest.
If you do not have a high school level of math fluency, you may skip this subtest.
This test is designed to assess your quantitative reasoning abilities rather than mathematical knowledge. However, questions will require basic mathematical fluency up to the high school level.
You may review the formula sheet below before starting the test.
Review formula sheet

items.question: In the figure above, what could be the value of S?
What is the total cost of 2 lbs of apples and 1 lb of pears?
If a car travels 20 miles in 30 minutes, how long will it take to travel 50 miles?
If x = 1, y = −1, and z = 2, what is the value of (x − y)/z?
Four apples in a box weighs 500 grams, and eight apples in a box weighs 900 grams. How much does the box weigh?
A class has 25 students, and 4/10 of them walk to school. How many students don't walk to school?
If a rectangle has a length of 5 and a perimeter of 30, what is its width?
What is ½ of ⅔ of ¾ of 60?
According to the time displayed on the clock, how many minutes remain until 4:24?
What is the positive difference between the largest single-digit square number and the largest two-digit square number?
Roy is reading a book with N pages. If each page has W words and Roy has X more pages left to read, how many words has he read so far?
The first three terms in an arithmetic sequence are x, x², and 28. What is the value of x?
Ethan starts running at 10 miles per hour and slows down 2 miles per hour after every hour. How long does it take Ethan to run 25 miles?
For a two-digit number XY, X@Y = (X − Y)(Y − X). For how many two-digit numbers is X@Y = 0?
Box A and B both have the same number of balls. If 4 balls are moved from box A to box B then box B will have twice the number of balls box A has. How many balls are there in total?
When you multiply all the whole numbers from 1 to 15 together, what is the last digit of the answer?
A bicycle wheel has 16 gaps between spokes. How many spokes does the bicycle wheel have?
The length of a train is 200 meters plus one-third of its length. How long is the train?
A coffee and a cake cost $5, a coffee and a sandwich cost $7, and a cake and a sandwich cost $4. How much does a coffee, a cake, and a sandwich cost?
The time is currently X minutes to Y. If it is 500 minutes after 12 o'clock, what is X + Y?
If m is an odd integer such that m = sqrt(240 + n), which of the following could be the value of sqrt(n)?
If x and y are positive single-digit integers such that x + y = 15, what is the difference between the greatest and least values of x − y?

On a "geometree", one-quarter of the leaves are square, 50% of the leaves are triangular, and the remaining leaves are hexagonal. In total, all the leaves have 20,000 sides. How many leaves does the geometree have?

The set P consists of all positive multiples of 7. The average (arithmetic mean) of four distinct numbers chosen from P is 42. If the smallest of these numbers is 14, what is the largest possible number chosen?

In a school, 75 percent of the students are enrolled in math, and 5 percent more students are enrolled in languages than in math. What is the difference between the minimum and maximum possible fraction of students who could be enrolled in both subjects?
A train located at point A needs to travel to point B. The train can travel along any of the given lines but cannot arrive at the same point twice. How many different paths can the train take?

Two cylindrical tanks are filled with water at the same uniform rate. Tank A has a radius 50 percent greater than Tank B and begins filling 1 hour before Tank B. Both tanks take 4 hours to completely fill. If Tank A starts filling at 8:52 a.m., at what time will their water levels be equal?
